THESE MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEALS HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED ON 5TH OCTOBER 2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT, THIS DAY,
UMESH M ADIGA J, PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Both these appeals arise out of common judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.235/2020 and MVC NO.236/2020 by the learned VIth Additional District Judge and MACT, Tumkur (herein after referred to as "Tribunal" for short) dated 22.04.2022.
Claimant in M.V.C.No.235/2020 has filed appeal in MFA No.6300/2022 and claimant in M.V.C.No.236/2020 has filed appeal in MFA No.6346/2022 for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
Both these matters are taken up together for disposal.
2. Even though these appeals are slated for hearing on admission and with the consent of the learned advocates for both sides, the appeals are taken up for final disposal.
3. We refer to the parties herein as per their rank before the Tribunal.

4. It is the case of claimants that on 03.11.2019, both the claimants along with their minor daughter were going on motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-44-U-0674 from Gandal to Yagachihalli road;
claimant in M.V.C.No.236/2020 - Nagaraju was riding said motor cycle and claimant on M.V.C.No.235/2020, Asharani H.G. who is wife of Nagaraj, was pillion rider along with their minor daughter Jeevitha.

At Bhadrarahinagundlu Cross, they met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Maruti Car bearing Registration No.KA-44-M-0769 by its driver; as a result of which, all the three riders of the motorcycle fell down and sustained injuries.

The claimant in M.V.C.No.235/2020, who was pillion rider in the NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB said motorcycle, had Nagaraju vs B Yogeshwara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164448958/
3 sustained grievous injuries.

She had taken treatment in Government hospital at Holiyar, District Government Hospital at Tumakuru and NIMHANS at Bengaluru and she had spent few lakhs towards medical expenses and she has been suffering from permanent disability.
With these reasons, she prayed to award compensation of Rs.50 lakhs.
The claimant in M.V.C.No.236/2020 contended that he had sustained grievous injury and taken treatment in Government Hospital.
He has been suffering from permanent disability.
He had spent huge money towards medical expenses.
He was aged about 40 years at the time of accident and is an agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to permanent disability he is unable to work and lost his earnings.
With these reasons prayed to award Rs.25,00,000/- as compensation.
Contention of respondent No.2 in both the cases are more or less similar.

6. Respondent No.2/Insurer has denied the contents of claim petition and it has contended that the accident had NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB taken place due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider and its liability is restricted to terms and conditions of policy of insurance and holding of valid and effective driving license by the driver of the offended car.
With these reasons, it prayed to dismiss the claim petitions.
7. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues for its consideration.

8. The Tribunal clubbed all the three claim petitions filed by rider, pillion rider and minor girl, who were going on the said motorcycle, that is clubbed M.V.C.Nos.234 of 2020, 235 of 2020 and 236 of 2020 and recorded common evidence.
The claimants had examined PWs-1 to 5 and got marked Exs.P1 to P25.

Respondent No.2 got marked policy of insurance as Ex.R1.
9.

The Tribunal, after hearing both the parties and on appreciating pleadings and evidence on record, by impugned judgment and award dated 22.04.2022, partly allowed M.V.C. No.235 of 2020 and 236 of 2020.

In MVC No.235/2020 the Tribunal assessed age of claimant as 25 years; her income as Rs.9000/- per month; applied multiplier as '18' and assessed her permanent disability to an extent of 45% and awarded total compensation of Rs.10,89,250/- under the following heads:
In M.V.C.No.236/2020 the tribunal has assessed the age of claimant as 40 years.

His income as Rs.9,000/- per month and disability at the rate of 9.3% and awarded following compensation.

Being aggrieved by the above said judgment and award, claimants in both the cases have filed these appeals for enhancement of compensation.
12. We have heard the learned advocates on both side.
The learned advocate for appellant/claimant has submitted that, claimant in M.V.C.No.235/2020 has been suffering from paraplegia, which is stated in the medical reports.
She is permanently disabled to an extent of 100% and she has been bedridden.
She is unable to do any type of work.
The Tribunal did not consider the said fact and without any basis, held that, claimant has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 45%.
The claimant in M.V.C.No.235/2020 was flower as well as vegetable vendor and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The Tribunal did not accept the same and without any basis, assessed her notional income as Rs.9000/- per month which is on much lower side.
The amount of compensation awarded under the other heads are meagre.

Therefore,
prayed for enhancement of compensation.
The learned advocate for Insurer has vehemently contended that, the Tribunal has not discussed or appreciated evidence available on record.
The evidence discloses that, claimant had personally appeared before the Court and gave her evidence.
It is not clarified either in her evidence or in the deposition of PW-3 that she was brought on stretcher or wheel chair, to the Court to give evidence.
She was cross-examined by the Insurer
and according to discharge summary given by the NIMHANS, her condition was stable and it is nowhere mentioned that she was bed-ridden or unable to move from the bed.
Claimant had examined PW-5 to prove her disability and according to the evidence of PW-5, the claimant has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 100%.

Nagaraju vs B Yogeshwara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164448958/
5

It is pertinent to note that in the cross-examination PW-5 admitted that she had not treated claimant immediately after the accident and for the first time, claimant had consulted PW-5 about two years after the alleged accident and PW-5 is unable to with-stand the cross-examination regarding assessment of disability of claimant.

Moreover, she is not a Neurophysician or Neurosurgeon and according to her affidavit-evidence, she is a Neuropsychologist and she is not competent to say about - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB neurological problem of the body and she might be an expert in saying the psychological condition of the patient.
Therefore, her evidence is not at all helpful to the Tribunal to assess the disability.
The learned counsel for Respondent No.2 has further vehemently submitted that the Tribunal ought to have appreciated these facts in the impugned judgment.
However, the Tribunal did not mention anything about the competency of PW-5 to give evidence or why the Tribunal assessed the disability of claimant as 45%.

Therefore, the impugned judgment of assessing the disability of claimant as 45%
is not at all tenable.
He further submits that it is true that the Insurer did not file any appeal against the impugned judgment.
However, any amount of compensation awarded should not be a bonanza to the claimants.
If they are deserving for the compensation, then to that extent can be awarded.
However, in the present case, the Tribunal without considering the facts, awarded exorbitant compensation.
Therefore, prayed to dismiss the appeal and recalculate the amount of compensation already awarded by the tribunal.

From the rival contentions of the parties, following question arises for our determination:
"Whether the claimant in both the cases is entitled for enhancement?"
15.

It is the case of the claimant that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the Car by its driver. PWs-1 and 3 have deposed before the Tribunal about rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
A criminal case was registered against the driver of the Car for causing accident in question.
The claimants have produced copies of documents, which were produced along with the charge-sheet in the Criminal Court against the driver of the Car.
Respondents are owner and insurer of the car, did not examine any witnesses to rebut the same.
In the cross-examination of PWs- 1 and 3, it was suggested that accident had taken place due to negligent riding of motorcycle by PW-1, the said suggestions were denied by PWs-1 and 3.
Moreover, respondents have not challenged the findings given against them regarding rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by its driver.

Therefore,
- 12 - Nagaraju vs B Yogeshwara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164448958/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB claimants had proved that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver and it does not call for any interference by this Court.
16. Assessment of compensation in MFA No.6300/2022:
In the claim petition, claimant has stated that her age at the time of accident was 25 years.
Claimant was examined as PW-3 and in her examination-in-chief, i.e., filed in the form of an affidavit, she had stated that her age was 30 years at the time of accident.
She had not produced any documents to prove her age.
In Ex.P11, her age is mentioned as 35 years.
In Ex.P12, her age is mentioned as 25 years.
In Ex.P14, her age is mentioned as 35 years.
In Ex.P15, her age is mentioned as 35 years and in Ex.P17, her age is mentioned as 30 years.
There is no consistency regarding age of claimant.
Under these circumstances, the age of claimant could be considered between 31 to 35 years for the purpose of application of multiplier.

17. Claimant, though in the pleading as well as in the evidence has contended that she was vending flowers as well - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB as vegetables and earning Rs.25,000/- per month, but there is no material on record either oral or documentary to prove it.
Therefore, the Court has to assess her notional income.
While settlement of motor vehicle claim petitions before the Lok- Adalath, notional income of a victim of an accident of the year 2019 is considered as Rs.14,000/- per month.
Same could be applied to the facts of the present case.

18. It is the contention of claimant before the Tribunal that, due to injuries sustained in the accident,
she has been bed-ridden and she has to carry all her daily pursuits on the bed and an attendant is required throughout the day to attend her daily pursuits.
She is wheelchair-bound and unable to move independently and she has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 100%.
Claimant had examined PW-5 Dr.Jamuna Rajeshwari.

According to the affidavit-evidence of PW-5,
she is professor of Neuropsychology, Department of Clinical Psychology, NIMHANS, Bengaluru.
"The claimant, aged about 35 years, approached her for neuropsychological assessment to neuropsychological unit on 21.03.2022.
The claimant was brought to hospital on the wheel-chair and the - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB claimant had significant locomotor disturbances in both upper and lower limbs.
Claimant had complained of significant pain in the whole body, which causes her to sit.
PW-5 clinically examined her and assessed her disability.
PW-5 assessed Vineland Social Maturity Scale (VSMS) was administered.
The assessment revealed significant deterioration in socio-adoptive functioning after head injury.

Claimant's social quotient on VSMS is 18.33, indicating profound Nagaraju vs B Yogeshwara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164448958/
7 impairment to 100% cognitive disability, according to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPWD) Act 2017.

sentences.text: It is also opined by the said doctor that patient need help in all her activities of daily living."

19. In her cross-examination, she had stated that "claimant visited her hospital for first time on the day of her clinical examination, i.e., about two to three years after the alleged accident dated 03.11.2019".
She had not treated the said claimant.
"According to her examination-in-chief, PW-5 clinically tested claimant only at the time of assessment of neuropsychological disability.
The claimant had not examined the doctor, who had treated her or atleast a Neurophysician or Neurosurgeon to assess her disability.
Therefore, the - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB submission of learned counsel for Insurer that evidence of PW- 5 is not of much assistance to the Tribunal to assess disability of claimant is tenable.
It is also worth to note that claimant had personally appeared before the Court and gave the evidence.
Nowhere in the evidence of PW.5, it is mentioned that on the day of evidence, she went to the Court on wheel-chair or even on stretcher.
The learned Presiding Officer of the MACT also did not note this facts in the deposition sheet.

During the course of arguments also, the learned advocate for appellant did not explain whether the claimant had appeared before the Court on the wheel-chair or without any difficulty attended the Court.

Except repeatedly submitting that patient has been suffering from paraplegia, the learned counsel for appellant did not explain the nature of disability of claimant on the basis of materials placed before the Tribunal.

20. In Ex.P11, i.e., discharge summary dated 07.12.2019 given by NIMHANS, it is stated at column diagnosis, "paraplegia due to L1 burst fracture with NL1-L3- - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB ASIA-C, with neurogenic bladder and bowel post-operative status (spinal fixation done)".

At the end of the said discharge summary, condition at the time of discharge of patient is mentioned, which reads as under:
"Patient is medically stable, afebrile, she is able to walk with a walker under one person supervision, minimally dependent for lower limbs, ADLs on caregiver, she is doing four-hourly SCIC has no leaks, she passes bowel regularly and has no accidents".
Thereafter, she was advised to contact the concerned doctor after three months.
There is no material on record to show that after three months, she had visited the said doctor or taken up any follow-up treatment.

Looking to these documents, which are not consistent with each other, it is difficult to accept that claimant has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 100% only on the basis of reference in Ex.P11 that "patient is paraplegic".

Had she examined the treated doctor or Nagaraju vs B Yogeshwara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164448958/
8 atleast the expert in the said neurological field, then, it could help the Tribunal to assess the proper disability.
The Tribunal ought to have considered these facts.

The Tribunal even did not appreciate these facts in the impugned judgment; as rightly submitted by the learned advocate for Insurer, except mentioning two paras and assessment of amount of compensation, nothing is discussed or appreciated by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has not at all considered oral and documentary evidence placed on record.

When a victim of an accident has been suffering from such grievous injuries and said to be suffering from paraplegia, at least the learned Presiding Officer of the Tribunal should have given much attention to such type of cases to assess just and reasonable amount of compensation.
Unfortunately, no such steps were taken by the Tribunal.
Therefore submission of learned advocate for appellant that appellant has been suffering for permanent disability to an extent of 100% is not acceptable.
Considering available medical records and the oral evidence of PW-5 and Ex.P11, it could be assessed that claimant has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 50% to the whole body.
The claimant has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 50%.
In view of the said reason, she had lost her future prospects, which needs to be added to her income.

In the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that 40% of income has to be added towards future prospects, if the victim of an accident is aged below 40 years.

sentences.text: In this case, as per the reasons stated above, age of the claimant is taken as between 31 to 35 years and hence future prospects of 40% has to be added to her income.
The multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 is '16' and same is to be applied.
The Tribunal had applied multiplier as '18' since it had taken age of claimant as 25 years.
Though the Tribunal held that claimant has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 45%, however, it did give benefits of future prospects, which needs to be awarded.

The claimant is entitled for following compensation under the head 'loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability':

23. Ex

. P11 shows that claimant had sustained L1 burst fracture with fracture of B/lamina and pedicles MRI D-L spine showed burst fracture of L1 vertebral body with a fracture of spinous process and right pedicle and B/L transverse process.
Motor power of all the limbs are mentioned in Ex.P11.
Considering the treatment mentioned in Ex.P11, it appears claimant had suffered severe pain and agony.
It appears, she underwent surgery of spine in NIMHANS Hospital at Bengaluru.

She was admitted on 03.11.2019 and discharged from the - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB NIMHANS Hospital on 07.12.2019, i.e., nearly more than a month she was admitted as inpatient in the said hospital and had been taken treatment.
Since she had sustained spinal injuries, it appears, someone might be attended her in the hospital and even after discharge from the hospital, someone might be attending her to follow daily pursuits.

According to contentions of PWs-3 and 5, claimant has been bed-ridden and daily pursuits, had been carried on the bed and someone is attending her in the house and she has been paying wages to the said labour.
Looking to contentions of claimant as stated by her in her evidence, it appears, she lost most of the amenities available to healthy person.
She lost normal life and marital enjoyment.
It appears she might not be in a position to take care of her minor child and enjoyment of motherhood.
Considering these facts, the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal on other heads are on lower side, which needs to be enhanced.

25.

The learned advocate for appellant has relied on following judgments rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court reported in the case of Pappu Deo Yadav Vs. Naresh Kumar & Others2 and in the case of Jagdish Vs. Mohan3 and also submitted that the Co-ordinate bench of this Court in the similar facts and circumstances of the case in MFA 2 AIR 2020 SC 4424 3 AIR 2018 SC 1347 - 22 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB No.2450/2018, in the case of Vittal Dandapur Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and another, decided on 15.06.2020 held that in case of paraplegia, the attendant charges of Rs.8,00,000/- and loss of amenities of Rs.3,00,000/- has to be awarded.

sentences.text: The said submission of learned advocate for appellant is not acceptable.
The amount of compensation depends upon different factors and facts and circumstances of each case.
In the present case, there is no proper pleading and evidence; the materials placed on record are not clear and very vague.
Considering these facts, compensation needs to be awarded.
The facts in the above said judgment are different and in that case it was proved that victim was suffering from 100% permanent disability.
Hence, same is not applicable to the facts of the present case.
The principle of law laid down in the case of Pappu Deo Yadav (referred supra) is considered and future prospects is considered while awarding compensation.
26. In this case, unfortunately, Tribunal did not appreciate the pleading and evidence available on record.
The claimant herself in her evidence has stated that she was aged - 23 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB about 30 years and the record shows that she was aged about 35 years.
However, the Tribunal has taken age of the claimant as 25 years on the basis of facts mentioned in the pleading, which is not supported by the claimant herself.
The Tribunal did not appreciate the evidence of PW-5 either to accept or reject her evidence.

The Tribunal did not note in the deposition as to whether the victim, i.e., the claimant came to the Court on wheel-chair or stretcher or without Nagaraju vs B Yogeshwara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164448958/
11 any difficulty.

The Tribunal could ascertain from PW-5, by asking a Court question, as to whether she was competent to assess the disability, i.e., neurological disability of claimant and even no questions were asked by the Court.

It is also worth to note that the learned advocate appearing for insurance company had cross examined the PW-5; except denial of her evidence, he did not question much regarding the physical disability of the victim.
Whatever disability stated by PW-5 is pertaining to psychological disability and not physical disability.
It is not the case of claimant in the claim petition or evidence of PW-3, that she has been suffering from psychological disability.
In view of these lapses of claimant as well as the Tribunal, this Court has to discuss in detail the facts and give findings in unusual way.
- 24 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB Assessment of Compensation in MFA No.6346 of 2022:
The claimant was rider of the motorcycle which met with an accident.
He underwent surgery.
He was inpatient in District Government Hospital, Tumakuru from 03.11.2019 to 22.11.2019, i.e., around 20 days.
The claimant was examined as PW-11 and he had stated about injuries sustained in the accident and difficulties due to the disability.
Petitioner has examined treated doctor as PW-4 and he has also stated about disability of the claimant.
PW-4 has stated about restrictions of movement of right leg and other difficulties of claimant and assessed his disability to right lower limb at 28% and to the whole body as 9.3%.
PW-4 has also - 25 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB stated that claimant required another surgery for removal of implants.
Claimant has pleaded that he was aged about 40 years at the time of accident and he was an agriculturalist and earning Rs.2 lakhs per annum.
The medical records produced by claimant also reveal that he was aged about 40 years at the time of accident.
However, he has not produced any other materials to prove his age.
Therefore, on the basis of available materials, his age has to be accepted as 40 years.

Nagaraju vs B Yogeshwara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164448958/
12
The claimant has not produced any documents to prove that he owns agricultural lands.
There are no other materials to believe that he is an agriculturalist and earning Rs.2 lakhs per annum.
Therefore, his notional income is to be determined.
The accident had taken place during the year 2019.

While settlement of motor vehicle claim petitions before the Lok-Adalath, notional income of a victim of an accident of the year 2019 is considered as Rs.14,000/- p.m., same could be applied to the facts in the present case.

The Tribunal has awarded following amount of compensation to the claimant:

The Tribunal has accepted age of the claimant as 40 years; permanent disability to the whole body as 9.3% and applied multiplier as '15'.
There is no dispute that multiplier applicable between the age group of 35 to 40 is '15' and same could be applied in the present case.
The Tribunal has accepted permanent disability of claimant as 9.3% as stated by PW-4 and it could be rounded off to 10%.
The amount of compensation awarded under other heads are inadequate.
The claimant had sustained fracture of both the bones of right leg.

However, the Tribunal has awarded Nagaraju vs B Yogeshwara on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164448958/
13 - 27 - NC: 2023:KHC:41717-DB compensation under the head 'loss of income during laid-up period' only for a period of a month.
Looking to the treatment taken by claimant and nature of injuries, it appears atleast for a period of three months, he could not be able to do any work.
As already stated above, about 20 to 21 days, he had taken treatment as inpatient in District Government Hospital at Tumakuru.
Therefore, the loss of income during laid-up period has to be considered for a period of three months.

Under these circumstances, the age of claimant could be considered between 31 to 35 years for the purpose of application of multiplier.
Therefore, the Court has to assess her notional income.
While settlement of motor vehicle claim petitions before the Lok- Adalath, notional income of a victim of an accident of the year 2019 is considered as Rs.14,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has not at all considered oral and documentary evidence placed on record.
When a victim of an accident has been suffering from such grievous injuries and said to be suffering from paraplegia, at least the learned Presiding Officer of the Tribunal should have given much attention to such type of cases to assess just and reasonable amount of compensation.
Considering available medical records and the oral evidence of PW-5 and Ex.P11, it could be assessed that claimant has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 50% to the whole body.
The Tribunal had applied multiplier as '18' since it had taken age of claimant as 25 years.

Considering these facts, compensation needs to be awarded.

Whatever disability stated by PW-5 is pertaining to psychological disability and not physical disability.
It is not the case of claimant in the claim petition or evidence of PW-3, that she has been suffering from psychological disability.
